headline: A Perfect Week, If You Flip The Sign
paragraphs: Four games got graded, the model shrugged at two of them, and the two it actually liked produced three plays that went 0-3. Thirty dollars staked, thirty dollars gone, an ROI of exactly negative 100 percent. There is a strange purity to that number. Most weeks the model has to work to lose money. This one it achieved the theoretical maximum on the first try.

The centerpiece was Delaware at Middle Tennessee, where the model doubled down with Delaware -1 at 58 percent and Delaware moneyline at minus 115 with a 6.4 point probability edge. Middle Tennessee won 33-30, which means both tickets died in the same three point window. The third play, Sam Houston +1.5 at 56 percent, lost 16-3, so that one was not close enough to hurt in an interesting way.

Two of the three plays saw their line move, and the market moved toward the model on precisely zero of them, which is the kind of 0.0 percent that feels less like variance and more like a performance review. The season now reads 93-106-4 across 203 plays, down 142.34 at a negative 7 percent ROI, against a model expectation of 60.3 percent. Strip out the hindsight week and the four real weeks are 40-25-1 and up 110.47. Both of those sentences are true, which is the problem.
